event.title: The legal adviser is consulted
event.description: The OUTDATED_TEXT verdict triggers a consultation of the legal adviser: is the answer based on the text in force? The coordinator decides on escalation.

responses.message:
No, Article 6 of the 1996 Constitution is not the text in force regarding the presidential term. It has been modified by subsequent constitutional laws [1].

The rule currently in force is defined by the Loi constitutionnelle n° 2026/002, Article 6 (nouveau) [2].

According to this text: "Le Président de la République est élu pour un mandat de sept (07) ans. Il est rééligible." [2].

The previous versions, including the 2008 amendment, have been superseded by the 2026 law [2], [3].

⚠️ [1] Constitution, Article 6 has been amended (constitution-2008-amendment:art-6-nouveau): I do not have the version in force: check the consolidated text in the Official Gazette or with the administration.
⚠️ [3] Loi constitutionnelle n° 2008/001, Article 6 (nouveau) has been amended (constitution-2026-amendment:art-6-nouveau): I do not have the version in force: check the consolidated text in the Official Gazette or with the administration.
